run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Querying the registered Elasticsearch target for indices matching 'app-184-*' returned 1800 matching indices. Exactly five of them report 500 documents each; every index ranked below them in the same sorted view reported 1 document (ranks 6-10 shown with docs.count=1). Because all five leaders are tied at 500 documents, their relative order is arbitrary, but the set of the five largest is unambiguous. Document counts are the state at the moment of the query; the tool has no time range, so this says nothing about the incident window.

claims.text: Elasticsearch holds 1800 indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' at the time of the query.

The five largest 'app-184-*' indices by docs.count, each with docs.count=500: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20, app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05, app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15. All five are tied at 500 documents, so their ranking order is arbitrary.

The next-ranked indices in the same sorted view report docs.count=1 (ranks 6-10: app-184-data-api-2024.01.18, app-184-data-api-2024.01.19, app-184-data-billing-2024.01.32, app-184-data-billing-2024.01.31, app-184-data-billing-2024.01.30), confirming no index below the top five exceeds 500 documents.

Store sizes of the five leaders as returned with the first query: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 47.8kb, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 46.9kb, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 45.8kb, app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 46.8kb, app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 30kb; all five report health=green and status=open.

An earlier aggregation attempt over the same pattern using jq '.docs.count' returned docs=null for all 1800 indices; the null was a jq field-path artifact (the key is literally 'docs.count'), and re-querying with .["docs.count"] returned the concrete document counts, so no index lacks a doc count in this view.

gaps: elasticsearch_list_indices has no time range; the counts describe the cluster at query time (observed 2026-11-21T08:34:41Z) and cannot show index sizes during the earlier part of the authorized window 2026-11-20T08:34:31Z to 2026-11-21T08:34:31Z.

Only the top 10 indices of the 1800 matching 'app-184-*' were displayed; document counts for the remaining 1790 indices were not individually read, though they are bounded by the 1-document values seen at ranks 6-10.
next_steps: If sizes are needed for a specific timestamp rather than the current state, consult an index-statistics history source (not available in this Run) instead of re-running the point-in-time index listing.
